articles.title: Billing — TryHackMe
articles.excerpt: Platform: TryHackMe · Difficulty: Medium · Category: VoIP / Command Injection / Privilege Escalation Today's target is Billing, a box built around MagnusBilling — an open-source VoIP billing platform…
articles.body: Platform: TryHackMe · Difficulty: Medium · Category: VoIP / Command Injection / Privilege Escalation Introduction Today's target is Billing , a box built around MagnusBilling — an open-source VoIP billing platform — sitting on top of the Asterisk PBX service it was written to invoice for. It's a good room for anyone who's only ever attacked generic CMS boxes, because the attack surface here is domain-specific: payment gateway integrations, call manager ports, a billing panel talking to a telephony backend. The foothold is a classic unauthenticated command injection in a third-party payment module — the kind of bug that shows up constantly in real deployments, because payment gateway plugins are bolted onto core applications by separate teams and reviewed far less rigorously.

articles.excerpt: FAQ blocks, HowTo toggles, and LocalBusiness cards in Rank Math or Yoast feel like free rich results. On small WordPress sites they more often create invisible FAQPage spam, the same FAQ JSON-LD on ev…
articles.body: FAQ blocks, HowTo toggles, and LocalBusiness cards in Rank Math or Yoast feel like free rich results. On small WordPress sites they more often create invisible FAQPage spam , the same FAQ JSON-LD on every URL , HowTo markup on pages that are not procedures , and LocalBusiness NAP that disagrees with the footer . That is schema hygiene — not a Schema.org encyclopedia, not title/meta SERP copy, and not image/Open Graph cards. It is how you stop wasting structured-data credibility (and, where Google still shows enhancements, rich-result eligibility) on markup nobody can see or trust. Honest 2026 note up front: Google no longer shows FAQ or HowTo rich results for ordinary sites (HowTo deprecated earlier; FAQ rich results fully wound down in 2026).

articles.body: What happened: Teams are splitting single monolithic agents into specialized sub-agents — a planner, a coder, a reviewer — coordinated by an orchestrator, instead of asking one agent to do everything in one long context. Why it matters: A single agent handling a long, multi-skill task tends to lose the plot: context gets crowded, early mistakes compound, and it's hard to tell which part of a bad output came from which reasoning step. Smaller, focused agents are easier to evaluate individually.

However, after the third lesson as well as an assignment, I worked with a hospital database of 15 patients. I have now realized the real power is in asking precise questions: Which patients have no insurance? Whose name starts with K? Who needs a phone call because there is no email on file? articles.title: Analog astronauts: How living underwater can prepare humans for space missions
articles.excerpt: How living underwater can prepare humans for space missions
articles.body: I have been dreaming of doing research in space as an astronaut my whole life, but for some reason, the thought of working underwater made me nervous. I’ve known for a long time that astronauts train underwater to simulate different scenarios they’re likely to experience in space. Diving was never an issue for me, either — I even made it as far as becoming a certified rescue diver. So what was the problem? This summer, I led a simulated space mission in an underwater habitat called the Jules’ Undersea Lab. It is a research station that is located 22 feet (6.7 meters) underwater near Key Largo, Florida. You have to scuba dive to get in and out of the station. To become an aquanaut , you have to stay underwater for at least 24 hours in a so-called state of saturation.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 26, 2004: Cassini spacecraft takes 1st-ever closeup photos of Saturn moon Titan
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 26, 2004, NASA's Cassini spacecraft took the first close-up images of Saturn's largest moon Titan. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 26, 2004, NASA's Cassini spacecraft took the first close-up images of Saturn's largest moon Titan. The Cassini spacecraft would later drop off a probe on Titan named Huygens, which was a European spacecraft that hitched a ride to the Saturn system with the Cassini mission. But before Cassini dropped off its robotic passenger, it flew by Titan a few times and took some amazing photos . Cassini completed its first flyby on July 3, 2004, but when it swung by a second time on Oct. 26, it got about 300 times closer than it did the first time. At the closest point of this flyby, Cassini was 745 miles (1,200 kilometers) away from the surface of Titan. The spacecraft took hundreds of photos during this flyby , and these were the highest resolution views of Titan anyone had ever seen.

articles.title: Magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor
articles.excerpt: Abstract: "Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires a universal gate set, but the necessary non-Clifford gates represent a significant resource cost for most quantum error correction architectures. M…
articles.body: Abstract: "Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires a universal gate set, but the necessary non-Clifford gates represent a significant resource cost for most quantum error correction architectures. Magic state cultivation offers an efficient alternative to resource-intensive distillation protocols; however, testing the proposal’s assumptions represents a challenging departure from quantum memory experiments. We present an experimental study of magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor. We implement cultivation, including code-switching into a surface code, and develop a fault-tolerant measurement protocol to bound the magic state fidelity. Cultivation reduces the error by a factor of 40, with a state fidelity of at least 0.9999(1) (retaining 8% of attempts).
